# Panel

Header: `winui/ui/panels/Panel.hpp`.

The shared base of the layout panels that own a list of children: [`Canvas`](canvas.md#uicanvas), [`WrapPanel`](wrap-panel.md#uiwrappanel), [`TilePanel`](tile-panel.md#uitilepanel), [`RelativePanel`](relative-panel.md#uirelativepanel) and [`LayoutPanel`](layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanel).

A panel owns its children by `std::unique_ptr` and hands callers back non-owning observers. It draws an optional background behind the children, plus a border with corner radius and padding on the panels that publish them, and lists the children for every tree-wide walk. Children draw in [`render_order()`](#render_order), which is insertion order unless the panel overrides it. The window hit-tests them topmost first in that order, so a press reaches only the topmost child under it. [`orphan()`](#orphan) takes a child back out alive. [`Panel`](#uipanel) cannot be constructed directly; derive from it and implement [`Element::measure_override()`](../tree/element.md#measure_override) / [`arrange_override()`](../tree/element.md#arrange_override), or use one of the panels above.

Example: 
```cpp
auto canvas = std::make_unique<ui::CanvasControl>();
canvas->set_background([](const ui::Theme& t) { return t.colors().background; });
canvas->set_background_transition(ui::BrushTransition{}); // blend on theme swaps
ui::ButtonControl* ok = canvas->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("OK"), 24.0f, 16.0f);
ok->on_click([] { /* ... */ });
for (const auto& child : canvas->children()) // insertion order
    child->set_margin(ui::Thickness{4.0f});
window.set_content(std::move(canvas)); // the window takes ownership of the panel and its children
```

## `ui::Panel`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

The shared base of the layout panels that own a list of children: [`Canvas`](canvas.md#uicanvas), [`WrapPanel`](wrap-panel.md#uiwrappanel), [`TilePanel`](tile-panel.md#uitilepanel), [`RelativePanel`](relative-panel.md#uirelativepanel) and [`LayoutPanel`](layout-panel.md#uilayoutpanel).

A panel owns its children by `std::unique_ptr` and hands callers back non-owning observers. It draws an optional background behind the children, plus a border with corner radius and padding on the panels that publish them, and lists the children for every tree-wide walk. Children draw in [`render_order()`](#render_order), which is insertion order unless the panel overrides it. The window hit-tests them topmost first in that order, so a press reaches only the topmost child under it. [`orphan()`](#orphan) takes a child back out alive. [`Panel`](#uipanel) cannot be constructed directly; derive from it and implement [`Element::measure_override()`](../tree/element.md#measure_override) / [`arrange_override()`](../tree/element.md#arrange_override), or use one of the panels above.

Example: 
```cpp
auto canvas = std::make_unique<ui::CanvasControl>();
canvas->set_background([](const ui::Theme& t) { return t.colors().background; });
canvas->set_background_transition(ui::BrushTransition{}); // blend on theme swaps
ui::ButtonControl* ok = canvas->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("OK"), 24.0f, 16.0f);
ok->on_click([] { /* ... */ });
for (const auto& child : canvas->children()) // insertion order
    child->set_margin(ui::Thickness{4.0f});
window.set_content(std::move(canvas)); // the window takes ownership of the panel and its children
```

### children_

```cpp
std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Element>> children_
```

The owned children in insertion order; derived panels read it in measure/arrange, append only through [`adopt_child()`](#adopt_child) and remove only through [`remove_child()`](#remove_child)/[`clear_children()`](#clear_children).

### children

```cpp
std::span<const std::unique_ptr<Element>> children() const
```

The owned children in insertion order (not necessarily drawing order, see [`render_order()`](#render_order)). The panel keeps ownership; the pointers stay valid for its lifetime.

### background

```cpp
const std::optional<Color>& background() const
```

The background, filled behind the children; nullopt (the default) draws nothing. Returns nullopt as well while a [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md) resource is set (see [`background_resource()`](#background_resource)).

### background_resource

```cpp
ThemeColor background_resource() const
```

The theme resource the background is drawn from, or null when a fixed color (or nothing) is set. A [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md) is re-read whenever the panel is drawn, so it follows theme changes without a setter call (ui/BackgroundBrush.hpp).

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(std::optional<Color> color)
```

Fixed background color; replaces any resource. Marks the panel for redraw.

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(ThemeColor resource)
```

Theme-resource background, e.g. `[](const Theme& t) { return t.colors().background; }`; replaces any fixed color. Marks the panel for redraw.

### background_transition

```cpp
const std::optional<BrushTransition>& background_transition() const
```

With a transition set, a later change of what the background draws (a new color, or a resource under a new theme) blends from the color on screen (Animation.hpp's [BrushTransition](../tree/brush-transition.md)). nullopt (the default) changes it at once.

### set_background_transition

```cpp
void set_background_transition(std::optional<BrushTransition> transition)
```

Enables (or, with nullopt, disables) the background blend; takes effect on the next change.

### orphan

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> orphan(const Element* child)
```

Takes `child` out of the panel alive and hands it back, for adding somewhere else. Focus inside it is cleared. Null when it is not one of this panel's children.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Lists the children in insertion order, the order [Tab](../controls/tabs.md#uitab) visits them.

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children in [`render_order()`](#render_order), not insertion order, so screen readers see them as they are stacked on screen (a [Canvas](canvas.md#uicanvas)'s z-index), and [hit_region()](../tree/element.md#hit_region) finds the topmost one.

### Panel

```cpp
Panel() = default
```

Only derived panels construct a [Panel](#uipanel); it starts empty, with no background or border.

### adopt_child

```cpp
Element* adopt_child(std::unique_ptr<Element> child)
```

Takes ownership of `child`, parents it and appends it. Returns the observer.

### remove_child

```cpp
bool remove_child(Element* child)
```

Removes `child`, an observer [adopt_child()](#adopt_child) returned, and lets it go. It is destroyed once the input or tick being handled has returned, since it may be the one whose handler asked for this. False when `child` is not one of this panel's children.

### clear_children

```cpp
void clear_children()
```

Removes and lets go of every child, as [remove_child()](#remove_child) does each.

### render_order

```cpp
virtual std::vector<Element*> render_order() const
```

The children in drawing order, bottom first. Pointer input is hit-tested in the reverse, topmost first.

### border_brush

```cpp
std::optional<Color> border_brush() const
```

The outline color; nullopt (the default) draws no border even with a non-zero [`border_thickness()`](#border_thickness). Nullopt as well while a [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md) is set.

### border_brush_resource

```cpp
ThemeColor border_brush_resource() const
```

The theme resource the border is drawn from, or null.

### set_border_brush

```cpp
void set_border_brush(std::optional<Color> color)
```

A fixed outline color; replaces any resource. Marks the panel for redraw.

### set_border_brush

```cpp
void set_border_brush(ThemeColor resource)
```

An outline color read from the theme each time the panel is drawn; replaces any fixed color. Marks the panel for redraw.

### border_thickness

```cpp
const Thickness& border_thickness() const
```

The border width in DIPs per side (default zero); it insets the children like padding.

### set_border_thickness

```cpp
void set_border_thickness(const Thickness& thickness)
```

Sets the border width; marks the panel for layout and redraw.

### corner_radius

```cpp
float corner_radius() const
```

The corner radius in DIPs, uniform for all four corners (default 0, square).

### set_corner_radius

```cpp
void set_corner_radius(float radius)
```

Sets the corner radius; marks the panel for redraw.

### padding

```cpp
const Thickness& padding() const
```

The padding in DIPs between the border and the children (default zero).

### set_padding

```cpp
void set_padding(const Thickness& padding)
```

Sets the padding; marks the panel for layout.

### content_inset

```cpp
Thickness content_inset() const
```

[Border](border.md#uiborder) plus padding, the inset taken off every side.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the background and border, then every child in [`render_order()`](#render_order).

### hit_test_children

```cpp
void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children in [`render_order()`](#render_order), topmost first.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the background transition, then ticks every child.
